title: Volumetric Video Takes Gold on the Live Events Stage
body_html:
What Was Announced

Volumetric video technology has been touted as a key component in the live events stage, with a recent development highlighting its potential for increased flexibility and scalability. The news suggests that volumetric video has achieved a significant milestone, winning a gold award in a live events competition. While the specifics of the award are not detailed, the announcement implies that volumetric video has demonstrated its capabilities in a high-pressure, live environment.

The Engineering and Operational Significance

The significance of this announcement lies in its potential to simplify operations and increase flexibility in live event production. Volumetric video technology allows for the capture and display of 360-degree video in real-time, which can be particularly useful in live events where multiple camera angles and perspectives are often required. By enabling the creation of immersive, interactive experiences, volumetric video can help to reduce the complexity of live event production, allowing engineers and operators to focus on other aspects of the production. Furthermore, the scalability of volumetric video technology means that it can be easily integrated into existing workflows, making it a valuable addition to any live event production team. The technical implications of this development are substantial. With volumetric video, live event producers can now capture and display a greater range of camera angles and perspectives, creating a more immersive experience for the audience. This requires significant advances in areas such as IP core networking, with SMPTE ST 2110 and AES67 playing key roles in enabling the transport of high-quality, low-latency video and audio over IP. Additionally, the use of volumetric video technology in live events will require significant investments in infrastructure, including high-performance computing, storage, and networking.

Industry Context

This development fits into a broader trend in the broadcast and media industry towards software-defined workflows and increased flexibility. As the demand for multi-platform delivery continues to grow, broadcasters and media companies are under pressure to simplify their operations and reduce costs. Software-defined workflows, which use software to automate and manage complex tasks, are becoming increasingly popular as a way to achieve this goal. Other approaches, such as the use of cloud-based services and artificial intelligence, are also being explored as a way to increase flexibility and reduce costs. In the context of live event production, the use of volumetric video technology is just one example of a broader trend towards increased flexibility and scalability. Other technologies, such as augmented reality and virtual reality, are also being explored as a way to create immersive experiences for live audiences. As the demand for live events continues to grow, it is likely that we will see further innovations in this area, as companies seek to create new and engaging experiences for their audiences.

Implications for Broadcast and Media Teams

For broadcast and media teams, this development highlights the need to consider the technical implications of new technologies and workflows. As volumetric video technology becomes more widely adopted, engineers and operators will need to be able to integrate it into existing workflows, ensuring that it does not introduce new complexities or bottlenecks. This will require significant investments in training and professional development, as well as a willingness to adapt to new technologies and workflows. Additionally, teams will need to consider the scalability and reliability of volumetric video technology, ensuring that it can be easily integrated into existing infrastructure and that it does not compromise the quality of the live event experience.
